title: Stronger Keys
author: Claude
blurb: Three short levels about a ladder of locks. A bronze key is worth 1, a silver key 2 and a gold key 3, and a door has a price of its own. A door opens when you can pay it and takes only its price, so a gold key opens a silver door and still has some left. Signs in the levels say how. Play it, then open it in Game-Maker and change a door's price.

box.tagline: A stronger key opens every weaker door.
box.back: A small explorer in a teal beanie finds bronze, silver and gold keys, each worth more than the last. A bigger key opens a smaller door and keeps the change, and small keys can add up to a big one. Read the signs, then open the game in Game-Maker and change a door's price.
features: Signs in the levels explain each idea
Keys add to a counter, doors take their price
Made to be copied and taken apart
